newsitem.title: USA: Calif. panel approves education funding bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. panel approves education funding bill.

text.p: A California legislative committee on Tuesday approved a bill that would stabilize higher education funding in the state and block future student fee increases, lawmakers said.
The state Assembly Higher Education Committee voted 9-to-0 in favor of Assembly Bill 1415, by Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante.
The bill would provide the California State University and University of California systems with yearly budget increases tied to annual gains in per capita personal income.

The bill would guarantee the two university systems the same proportional share of the state general fund budget as they now receive, along with additional funding to cover the cost of enrollment growth.

Future student fee increases would be eliminated unless specifically called for by future legislatures, Bustamante said. Even then, fee increases would be limited to growth in per capita personal income.

"AB 1415 affirms the state's long-term commitment to quality higher education and does it without hurting other areas of the budget or doing economic harm to students and their families," Bustamante said in a statement.
